feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV with clear senior-level progression, relevant digital leadership scope, and good use of scale indicators. It reads professionally and is well aligned to communications/strategy roles, but it would be stronger with tighter formatting, fewer repeated skill sections, and more outcome-focused achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director and consulting roles, which strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Strong breadth across digital strategy, web platforms, analytics, email, social, and multimedia; the profile and experience sections align well.  
- Good use of concrete scope markers such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers,” which adds impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: include results like engagement growth, email performance, cost savings, process efficiency, campaign impact, or audience growth.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these would improve structure and make the CV feel sharper.  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is slightly inconsistent (e.g., missing serial commas in some places); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead. No obvious misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning for senior digital communications roles. It reads polished, but it stays fairly generic and overlaps heavily with the competencies and work experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and add the missing apostrophe: “12 years’ experience.”
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: senior digital strategy leadership, Drupal/web modernization, and advocacy/public-sector communications.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a sharper value proposition tied to mission-driven organizations.
- Consider a rewrite such as: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web modernization, cross-channel communications, and content operations for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in Drupal platforms, editorial workflow design, analytics, and stakeholder coordination. Known for translating complex policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content and scalable digital systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” and advocacy messaging are reinforced throughout the NACo experience, so keep the intro concise.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership/operations capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multichannel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Prioritize strategic/lead-level strengths over generic coordination language; e.g., replace “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” with “Cross-functional leadership & governance.”
- Consider a sharper version: Digital strategy & transformation • Multichannel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial systems & governance • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Analytics & performance reporting • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Keep style consistent: use either “multichannel” or “multi-channel” throughout the CV, and prefer “communications” over “communication” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and Topline/Technical sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a broad service list. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, and web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-oriented line: “Improved cross-channel publishing workflows, governance, and analytics to support coordinated web, email, social, and multimedia communications.”
- Recast Drupal/CMS work to emphasize deliverables and value: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable toolkits for member engagement.”
- Make the AI/search bullet the standout item and add a measurable goal if available: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX to improve access to policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating governance, analytics, and enterprise web modernization language already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Technical troubleshooting” undersells this senior role; replace with higher-level phrasing like optimization, implementation, or platform enhancement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with highest-impact achievements: Drupal migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, governance improvements.
- Make outcomes more measurable where possible: add team size, budget, traffic growth, email performance, production volume, cost savings, or faster publishing/reporting cycles.
- Tighten channel bullet to emphasize strategic ownership, not routine management: “Oversaw multi-channel communications reaching tens of thousands of county officials” rather than listing each platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/newsletter and recurring video language overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Governance/editorial systems also appear in the summary and consultant role; use distinct wording or quantify the operational change here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, cadence, cross-team coordination, and channel-building.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day multi-channel communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video platforms, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around channel creation: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency across digital output.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “Produced weekly video updates” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager / Producer role and footer project; keep the emphasis here on formalizing it as a recurring channel.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong theme alignment with the candidate’s recent leadership roles, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the strategic scope and emphasize enterprise/public-sector context.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to recent work:  
  **Enterprise digital strategy • Editorial governance & publishing operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy messaging • Audience-centered content strategy**
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “publishing operations” or “content operations” to better match the work experience language.
- If space allows, make one phrase more outcome-oriented, e.g. **Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications**.
- Keep this section strategic; leave channel execution, analytics, and AI/search specifics to the other Topline Skills groups.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long list to a sharper, impact-oriented grouping: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles; they are already covered in Technical + IT.
- Replace “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” with “CMS Platforms, Integrations & Automation” for clearer positioning.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-linked: “AI-enabled search and discovery experiences” aligns well with the recent legislative search project.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep topline skills strategic, not exhaustive.
- “CMS modernization” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Enterprise website modernization.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use a tighter mix of platforms and business skills: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Consider replacing one tool with a stronger impact-oriented phrase such as “measurement architecture” or “insight-driven optimization.”
- Keep the most credible/recent tools tied to NACo work; GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Clarity are enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies unless phrased more distinctly.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo role bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and technical depth rather than repeating broad terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented, tighter phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- PTZ camera and studio system operation
- Virtual event production workflows
- Consider renaming the heading to “Video, Studio & Live Event Production” for sharper differentiation.
- If accurate, add scale/scope instead of generic labels, e.g., “multi-camera livestreams,” “recurring advocacy video programming,” or “in-house studio production.”
- Keep terms parallel and noun-based; avoid mixing broad categories (“studio operations”) with formats (“hybrid and virtual event production”) unless all bullets describe capabilities at the same level.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” substantially repeat Core Competencies and Work Experience language.
- “Video production and editing” is also echoed in Technical + IT (“Premiere Pro… Podcast production”) and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a recent senior digital leader, this item should signal level of ownership or specialization, not just names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint / Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to actual use: e.g., **Drupal 10**, **enterprise publishing**, **campaign microsites**, **intranet/collaboration**
- Keep only platforms here; avoid mixing in modernization language already covered elsewhere
- Consider shortening further to: **CMS & Web Platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one version more strategic and this one purely technical
- “Drupal” is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same unsupported list format

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic coding terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **JavaScript (ES6+) • HTML/CSS • jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI/CD**
- Drop versioned/basic terms like **HTML5** and **CSS3** unless required by the role; they add little value at this level.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work: **Drupal front-end implementation**, **serverless scripting**, or **deployment automation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears in Topline Skills; keep the fuller phrasing in one place only.
- **API integrations** and **workflow automation** also overlap with Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so this section should stay tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and keep only strongest, most relevant tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Remove lower-value/general tools unless heavily used in recent roles: Basecamp, Trello
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied capability: “workflow design,” “cross-team planning,” or “process automation”
- Example rewrite: “Automation & Workflow Systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; this section should stay tool-focused, not repeat concepts.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; keep only if they support your systems/operations leadership story.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email platform ownership, campaign execution, or audience engagement use cases.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**.
- Expand the phrasing slightly to show function: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience journeys)**.
- If accurate, prioritize the platform most tied to recent work first; if NACo primarily used one system, list that first for stronger relevance.
- Consider adding one measurable qualifier elsewhere in the CV tied to these tools, such as newsletter volume, audience size, or campaign cadence, rather than here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets already covering email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; avoid repeating audience-size claims in this skills line.
- “Engagement” may blur with broader multi-channel communications already covered in Core Competencies.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with clearer scope and any available output metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Add concrete outputs where possible: number/frequency of livestreams, weekly video series cadence, website refresh scope, email/social volume, or audience growth.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with specific actions and results.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content across web, email, social and multimedia, including livestreams and a weekly video update. Standardized day-to-day publishing workflows and provided direct oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video update” and workflow improvements overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on foundational buildout and production.
- Avoid repeating broad channel ownership already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and use stronger action/result framing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Cut vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” unless you can specify outputs (e.g., articles, videos, campaign assets, stakeholder audiences).
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, series length, audience, or teams/programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia production; later roles already cover video, digital operations and channel leadership more strongly.
- Don’t repeat “first” team-building language here, since the 2015–2018 role already covers creation of the in-house digital team.
